about: Sources for /el-nino-and-cities/ ('El Niño and India's smaller cities: preparing for summer 2027'), a practical preparedness guide for smaller cities across India. Official outlooks (NOAA, WMO, IMD) are dated as issued; India-level research is described with its limits; NIUA learning notes are cited with their printed page numbers. Nothing here forecasts a city's heatwave or flood. Built 18 November 2026; revised the same day.

claims.text: NOAA's discussion of 12 November 2026 keeps an El Niño Advisory in effect: a strong-to-very strong El Niño is likely through January-March 2027 (greater than a 79% chance), expected to begin weakening in early 2027; the next discussion is due on 10 December 2026.
NOAA publishes each new discussion at the same address.

WMO's Update (3 September 2026) gave a nearly 100% likelihood that El Niño persists through February 2027, and says the strength of an El Niño does not by itself determine how severe its impacts are in any one country.
rests_on: does not determine how severe its impacts will be in any individual country

claims.text: IMD: rainfall over India in the 2026 southwest monsoon was 87% of its long period average, with July at 101%.
IMD releases its seasonal outlooks for the hot season between March and May.
IMD recorded very heavy rainfall over Marathwada in the 24 hours to the morning of 30 September 2026.
IMD publishes district-wise warnings, and its regional centres in Nagpur and Mumbai publish forecasts for Maharashtra.

In India's records for 1961-2013, most years with above-normal heatwave activity in the April to June season followed El Niño events; the study also links heatwaves to the Indian Ocean and to dry soils.
rests_on: years following the El Nino events
alts: years following the El Nino events

claims.text: Over central India, widespread extreme rain events rose threefold in 1950-2015 even as total rainfall declined.
rests_on: threefold increase in widespread extreme rain events over central India
alts: threefold increase in widespread extreme rain events over central India

claims.text: Practical Action Nepal has used seasonal forecasts to guide early action, working with media and local partners on awareness and supporting heat action planning (June 2026).
rests_on: Practical Action Nepal has been using seasonal forecasts

claims.text: In Peru, with the Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation, the national civil defence institute (INDECI) and local government, Practical Action set out early action to protect 1,500 families from floods and mudslides.
rests_on: Swiss Agency for Development and Cooperation

claims.text: Maharashtra's State Heat Action Plan 2024 names Vidarbha, Marathwada and Khandesh as the most vulnerable regions and 15 districts as high-risk, and includes cooling centres and reserved hospital beds.
The state plan lists Akola, Jalgaon and Nanded among its districts.

NCDC's advisory for summer 2026 asked state health departments to report heatstroke cases and deaths daily from 1 March 2026, to consider public cooling and drinking water facilities, and to use local death records for local early warning thresholds.
rests_on: Advisory for State Health Departments for Summer 2026
public cooling and drinking water facilities

claims.text: NIUA's Learning Note 1: informal settlements face higher exposure to heat, flooding and water scarcity (p. 33); smaller towns often have limited resources and capacities (p. 35); public spaces can become safe zones during heatwaves (p. 85).
NIUA's Learning Note 2: city-scale resilience planning moves beyond isolated projects (section 2.6, p. 40); Table 2 pairs outputs with outcomes (p. 54).
rests_on: Output and outcome indicators for various adaptation actions in urban context

claims.text: NDMA's 2025 guidelines for cooling centres cover site selection in high-risk areas, retrofitting, and operations and maintenance.

WMO's Global Seasonal Climate Update, released 26 October 2026, forecasts that tropical Pacific sea surface temperatures may rise to 3.8 °C above average during November 2026 to January 2027, and says the event could be unprecedented in strength.
IMD works through Regional Meteorological Centres, assisted by Meteorological Centres at the state level that disseminate advisories and warnings about regional weather.
rests_on: Meteorological Centers (MCs) at the state level

claims.text: Under Jodhpur's heat action plan, a net zero cooling station designed for the informal sector was installed in a high-risk ward identified through ward-level risk assessment, and IMD heat alerts were translated into locally accessible formats and passed on through community-based channels.

Kerala's government allocated ₹1 crore to each District Collector for heat protection measures such as drinking water kiosks and cooling centres, and directed local bodies to develop decentralised heat action plans.
Uttar Pradesh introduced district-specific heatwave thresholds that classify alerts as yellow, orange or red based on regional climatic conditions.
A 2018 evaluation, as reported in NRDC's review, found Ahmedabad's heat action plan may have contributed to approximately 1,190 fewer deaths per year on hot days after full implementation.
The Thane heat action plan highlights that extreme warm nights are projected to increase more than extreme hot days, with felt temperatures higher than dry temperatures because of humidity.

NIUA's Learning Note 1 notes that informal settlements face disproportionately higher exposure to heat, flooding and water scarcity, and points to entry points for climate action within municipal functions.
rests_on: entry points for climate action within municipal functions

claims.text: In April 2024 the city corporation and its partners opened a net-zero cooling station in a heat-vulnerable ward of Jodhpur North identified through the heat action plan's vulnerability assessment.
Jodhpur's 2023 heat action plan sets out passing warnings by SMS and WhatsApp and estimating local thresholds.
In March 2026 Kerala decided to allocate ₹1 crore to each district collector for summer measures and asked officials to set up drinking water kiosks where people gather.
rests_on: Rs 1 crore each to district collectors

claims.text: Uttar Pradesh's disaster management authority derived yellow, orange and red alert temperatures for each of its 75 districts from percentiles of each district's temperature record; its 2024 heat plan sets out the method, first drafted for Agra.
rests_on: District Wise Heat Wave Threshold Determination

claims.text: A 2018 evaluation estimated about 1,190 average annualized deaths avoided after Ahmedabad's heat action plan was implemented.
